_comment: HAND-AUTHORED cross-surface wire fixture for the chat live-document stream (mobile charter D59). This file, not any implementation, is the contract: the server emitter must MATCH it and every client consumer must reach the recorded outcomes. It lives in internal/pdrender/testdata/ because that is the one path bound by mobile.yml AND go-tests.yml AND the Elixir dispatcher at once, so a regen re-fires all three consumers (the chat_golden_toolrows.json precedent). Consumers today: internal/pdrender/chat_stable_frames_test.go (Go/TUI) and apps/mobile/__tests__/stableFrameContract.test.ts (mobile). Edit the contract here first, then both consumers.

contract._note: Both frames are id-LESS and ALWAYS carry a data: line. The payload is JSON, NEVER raw markdown: the Go SSE reader TrimSpaces every data line while the mobile reader strips only one leading space, so raw text would differ per surface.
contract.why_to: REQUIRED: a client cannot advance a byte cursor from {from, blocks} alone -- block text is not source bytes (53 source vs 42 derived over four segments in the run proof), so a PERFECT stream gets rejected at frame 2 without it.
contract.why_turn: REQUIRED: `from` alone FALSE-ACCEPTS across a turn boundary, and the client's own `gen` cannot fence it (gen advances on system/init, not on the event: message replay that CAUSES the gap). Sequence turn_boundary_gap_false_accepted_by_from_only is the run proof.
contract.why_skeleton_is_server_side: The classifier is part of the one converter, so every surface draws the same placeholder for the same unsettled tail.
contract.what_skeleton_prose_is: skeleton.prose is the PROSE ABOVE the forming component -- the bytes between `to` and the component's first triggering line -- NOT a caption and NOT the component's own body. It is the StreamTail.classify/1 third element verbatim (Barkpark.StudioChat.StreamTail, charter D62/D67): the client renders it as live text ABOVE the placeholder box so a paragraph that happens to sit under a forming table keeps streaming. It is legitimately the EMPTY STRING whenever the component starts exactly at `to`, and a consumer must accept that -- never require it non-empty.
contract.why_stable_end_is_its_own_event: The capped state is reachable with ZERO stable frames ever emitted (run-proven at a 4 KiB cap: one unbroken block yields capped with 0 segments), so there is no stable frame to carry a terminal field.

offsets._note: from/to are UTF-8 BYTE offsets into the turn's source markdown, half-open [from,to). Every `sources` string here is deliberately pure ASCII so byte length equals UTF-16 length and the SAME bounds assertion holds in Go and in TypeScript; a fixture regen that introduces non-ASCII must teach the mobile consumer to measure bytes.
offsets.cursor_rule: STRICT (the D59 contract): on a stable frame, if data.turn != current turn, adopt it and reset the cursor to 0; then accept iff data.from == cursor and set cursor = data.to. On stable_end: adopt/reset the turn the same way; reason=degraded drops all segments (cursor := 0, `from` NOT checked, render the persisted row); otherwise accept iff data.from == cursor. A mismatch is a GAP: keep what is committed, render the remainder plain, stop trusting the segment stream for this turn.
offsets.from_only_rule: The NAIVE predicate D59 rejects, recorded here only so the discrimination can be RUN rather than asserted: identical, except it never reads data.turn and therefore never resets the cursor on a turn change. `expected_from_only` is present on exactly one sequence -- the one where the two disagree.
offsets.committed_bytes: The cursor at the end of the walk, scoped to final_turn (a turn change resets it), or 0 when the server degraded.

sequences.why: The happy path: contiguous [from,to) segments, no skeleton, stable_end reason=settled whose from equals the committed total. Note frame 1's block text (17 chars) is nowhere near its 22 source bytes -- the reason `to` exists at all.

sequences.name: open_fence_skeleton
sequences.title: A segment carrying an open-fence skeleton
sequences.why: Frame 0 settles the lead paragraph while an unterminated ``` fence is still streaming past `to`. The server classifies the remainder (skeleton.kind=code) because the classifier lives in the one converter (D59); the client draws a code-shaped placeholder, never a raw half-fence. skeleton.prose is the line ABOVE the fence -- the bytes from `to` up to the fence's first line -- so that prose keeps streaming as live text while only the fence is hidden behind the placeholder (see contract.what_skeleton_prose_is). Frame 1 settles both the held-back paragraph and the closed fence, and the skeleton goes null. The settled code block carries `lang: "go"` -- the fence info string, which FromMarkdown emits as `lang` ONLY when the fence supplies one (a language-less fence keeps the two-key {type, value} map). Nothing asserts block equality against this file, so that key was HAND-added here (bl-frommarkdown-fence-language) rather than forced by a red test: this fixture is the contract, and a contract that lags the emitter is the silent drift the fixture exists to refuse.

sequences.name: midstream_gap_one_frame_dropped
sequences.title: A GAP: the middle frame of a three-segment turn is removed
sequences.why: The recorded stream is the clean one MINUS frame 1. The survivor's from (59) does not equal the cursor (14), so the client degrades: keep everything committed so far, render the remainder as plain text, stop trusting the segment stream for this turn. Both predicates catch this one -- it is the baseline, not the discriminator.

sequences.name: turn_boundary_gap_false_accepted_by_from_only
sequences.title: A TURN-BOUNDARY gap where turn 1's total coincidentally equals the survivor's from
sequences.why: Turn 1 settles at 131 bytes. Turn 2's opening frame (0 -> 131) is LOST, and turn 2's second frame starts at 131 -- the same number. A from-only cursor (which cannot see a turn boundary it was never told about, because `gen` advances on system/init and not on the message replay that causes the gap) accepts it and splices turn 2's tail onto turn 1's message. The turn-plus-from cursor resets on the turn change and rejects at from=131, want 0. THIS is why `turn` is on the wire.

sequences.name: capped_after_zero_stable_frames
sequences.title: stable_end reason=capped with ZERO stable frames ever emitted
sequences.why: One unbroken block larger than the segment cap settles nothing at all, so the terminal state arrives with the cursor still at 0. This is the run-proven reason stable_end is a DISTINCT EVENT rather than a field on a stable frame: there is no stable frame to hang it on. The client must render the persisted row and show no partial document.

sequences.name: degraded_after_two_segments
sequences.title: stable_end reason=degraded after two good segments
sequences.why: The SERVER declares its own segmentation untrustworthy. Unlike a client-detected gap (which keeps what it committed), degraded means the client DROPS its segments outright and renders the persisted row -- so the committed cursor goes back to 0 and `from` on the terminal frame is not cursor-checked. Distinguishing the two is the whole point of carrying the reason.

sequences.name: unknown_future_fields_tolerated
sequences.title: Unknown future fields on both frame kinds
sequences.why: Every consumer ignores keys it does not know (the Go decoder's existing tolerance, mirrored on mobile), so a server that starts stamping `hint`, `cost` or `trace_id` does not degrade an older client. A consumer that rejects on unknown keys reds HERE rather than in production.
